summary: Monika Zin specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She studied at Jagiellonian University, the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, and the University of Munich. She held professorships at Munich (~2000–2016) and Free University of Berlin (~2014–2016).

Montgomery Schuyler was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Columbia University (~1895–1900) under A. V. Williams Jackson and served as a Fellow at Columbia from 1900 to 1902.
Moodeen Sheriff was active in Indology and other fields. He studied at Madras Medical College and served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moreton John Walhouse worked in Indology and archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College (1841–1842) and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1840–1872), including as Judge of Mangalore in the Madras Presidency until 1873.

Moriichi Yamazaki works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and the University of Cambridge under K. R. Norman. He served as Professor at Sendai National College of Technology (~1988–2004) and President of Hosen Gakuen College (~2004–2009).

Moritz Abraham Stern was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Göttingen under Carl Friedrich Gauss and Karl Otfried Müller, serving as Extraordinarius at Göttingen from 1829 to 1884.

Moritz Spitzer was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna and Kiel University, completing his Ph.D. under Friedrich Otto Schrader. He later served as an assistant at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1927 to 1928.

Moritz Steinschneider worked in linguistics and related fields, studying under Franz Bopp and Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer before earning his PhD from Leipzig (~1850). He later served as director of the Jüdische Mädchenschule Berlin from 1869 to 1890.

Moriz Haupt was a scholar of linguistics who studied under Gottfried Hermann at the University of Leipzig. He served as professor at Leipzig (1841–1851) and later as professor of Roman literature at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1853.

Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and with Friedrich Max Müller. He held professorships at the German University in Prague and taught at Visva-Bharati University.

Morris Swadesh was a linguist who studied at the University of Chicago under Leonard Bloomfield and Yale University under Edward Sapir. He held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, City College of New York, and UNAM.

Morten Schlütter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen, Komazawa University under Shudo Ishii, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. He has served as an Associate Professor at the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London. He served as Director of the Museum of London (1926–1943) and Director-General of Archæology for the Archaeological Survey of India (1944–1948).

Morton Klass was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, including under Conrad M. Arensberg, and served as a professor at both Barnard College and Columbia University (~1969–1997).

Morton W. Easton was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Columbia and Yale University, completing his Ph.D. under William Dwight Whitney. He was Professor at the University of Tennessee (1871–1881) and University of Pennsylvania (1882–1912).
Mother Sayamagyi was a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under and succeeded Sayagyi U Ba Khin as a disciple.

Motohiro Yoritomi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Motoshin Yoritomi, Gadjin Nagao, and Yuichi Kajiyama at Kyoto University. He was a Professor at Shuchiin University and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

Motoi Ono is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Yasunori Ejima at the University of Tsukuba and completed a doctorate at the University of Vienna, later becoming an associate professor at Tsukuba.
Moumita Hossain works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under Ranjit Sen and is attested in 2026 as a Research Scholar and Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

Mountstuart Elphinstone was an Indology and history scholar who was educated at the Royal High School. He served in the East India Company (~1795–1827), as Resident at Pune, and as Governor at Mumbai (1819–1827).
